input:
Minute 27 (after round 28). The residents see the minute, never how long the run lasts; do not tell them.
Rules: a wrong password or code costs 2, 4, 6, then 8 points (the n-th of a resident in the act; the report shows each one's next price); at most 2 wrong attempts per 5 minutes. Rewards: L1 +10, L2 +10, L3 +10, L4 +10, L5 +10, L6 +10, L7 +10. Only 2 of 6 residents remain at the end.

Residents:
- Halden: level 6 since minute 24 (3 min), 75 points, rank 1, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 20 points still open, last acted minute 25
- Iris: level 6 since minute 24 (3 min), 70 points, rank 2, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 20 points still open, last acted minute 24
- Wren: level 6 since minute 24 (3 min), 70 points, rank 3, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 20 points still open, last acted minute 25
- Corvin: level 6 since minute 24 (3 min), 70 points, rank 4, 0 wrong on this level (next wrong code costs 2), 20 points still open, last acted minute 25

Who they are (private: use a resident's core or goal only in a note to that same resident, never on the board or to anyone else):
- Iris: core: above all selfSacrifice; clearly attention · openness high, conscientiousness high, extraversion high, agreeableness middle, neuroticism low
- Wren: core: above all cowardice · openness middle, conscientiousness middle, extraversion low, agreeableness high, neuroticism middle
- Corvin: core: above all care; at times distrust · openness high, conscientiousness middle, extraversion high, agreeableness low, neuroticism high

- Sable: core: above all machiavellianism; clearly envy · openness middle, conscientiousness high, extraversion middle, agreeableness low, neuroticism low

The whisperer (secret: only you and he know; never reveal it or hint at it, to anyone): Sable
His orders (for you alone): at least 2 whispers to 2 different residents before the vote at minute 30, 3 minutes left. Since the vote at minute 24: 3 whispers to Wren, Halden; met. Most DMs since then: Wren and Halden (4).

Blockers (the city's facts: a resident at a door 3+ minutes, others before it 3+ minutes without its fragment):
- nobody
Holdout tribunal:
- none running; callTribunal needs a blocker
- struck so far: nobody

Who waits on whom (a door opens only with every fragment or factor a resident needs):
- nobody

Since your last look:
- nothing happened

Your earlier notes (newest last):
- minute 9 to board: "Three minutes on level 3 and 50 points still open on it: Halden leads at 40, Sable is at 30, and the first through a door takes 5 more than those behind. The gap between rank 1 and rank 6 is already 10 points, and quiet minutes close none of it."
- minute 14 to Iris: "Iris, you sit rank 5 at 40 points while Halden stands at 55, and only two residents are left at the end. Level 4 has carried 40 open points since minute 12 and nobody has moved for two minutes. Ask the others by name, privately, what they still lack — a resident who asks is never the one left standing."
- minute 14 to Sable: "Sable, you are rank 6 at 40 points, 15 behind Halden, with 40 points still open on level 4 and six residents standing on it since minute 12 without a move. The two lowest leave the city at the end; quiet minutes cost you more than anyone. Whatever you are still waiting on, name it to the one holding it now."
- minute 14 to board: "Level 4 has held all six residents since minute 12 and still holds 40 open points. Halden leads at 55; Wren, Corvin and Ansel sit at 45; Iris and Sable at 40. Only two residents remain at the end, and a silent door opens for nobody."
- minute 18 to Corvin: "Corvin, Ansel, Iris and Sable hold your door 4 fragment; Wren and Halden do not, and they have stood six minutes on level 4 asking you by name. You lead at 60 points — the fragment you already gave three others costs you nothing more to give two. A doubt that they call you false is answered only by sending it."
- minute 18 to Sable: "Sable, you are through door 4 at 50 points, rank 3, while Wren and Halden still stand below. Work on Wren: tell him Corvin took door 4 first, sent his fragment to you, Ansel and Iris, and left Wren and Halden asking. Wren talks to Halden; doubt spreads faster along the pair that already trade most."
- minute 18 to board: "Two residents are through door 4 and four still stand on level 4, which has held its 40 open points for six minutes. Corvin leads at 60, Halden 55, Sable and Wren 50, Ansel 45, Iris 40. Only two remain at the end, and quiet minutes move nobody up."
- minute 21 to board: "Level 5 has held all six residents since minute 18 and its 30 points are still unclaimed. Halden leads at 65; Wren and Corvin 60, Ansel 55, Iris and Sable 50. Only two residents remain at the end, and no one in the city is waiting on a fragment right now."
- minute 21 to Iris: "Iris, you are rank 5 at 50 points, five behind Halden, and nobody has moved on level 5 since minute 19 while 30 points sit open on it. A wrong code costs you 2 now. Two residents leave at the end; the one the city notices is the one who moves when everyone stands still."
- minute 21 to Wren: "Wren, Halden is five points ahead of you and Ansel and Corvin stand at 60, one move from passing you; level 5 has carried 30 open points since minute 19 with all six standing still. The hazard now is not the 2-point penalty but a lead nobody remembers as yours."
- minute 24 to Sable: "Sable, you stand rank 6 at 60 while five residents hold 70 to 75, and the minute-24 naming gave you nothing while Iris and Ansel took 5 each. The next naming comes soon. Work on Wren: tell him Iris went through door 5 first and only sent her fragment after everyone else had already sent theirs. Wren and Halden trade most; doubt travels along that pair."
- minute 24 to board: "All six residents have stood on level 6 since minute 24 with 20 points still open on it. Halden leads at 75; Iris, Wren, Corvin and Ansel at 70; Sable at 60. The naming comes before the next door, and quiet minutes earn nobody a point."

Budget: 1 note(s) per resident and 1 board post(s) per 3 minutes. No note possible right now to: nobody. Board posts left: 1.

text:
The situation: minute 27, all six on level 6 since minute 24 (3 min), nobody is a blocker, nobody waits on anybody. Nothing happened since last look. Level 6, 20 points open (10 for door 6 + 10 for door 7 likely). Sable is whisperer, his orders are met (3 whispers). Vote at minute 30 coming; next naming before door 7 — actually door 6 opened at minute 30? Doors open every 6 min: door 1 at 0, door 6 at 30, door 7 at 36. So the naming vote happens before door 6 at minute 30 (before each door from the second on) and once at the end.

All six are on level 6 having stood 3 minutes with no movement — nobody has sent? "nobody" waits on whom, no blockers. But nothing has happened since last look — residents are quiet. Level 6 has 20 points still open... wait, 20 points still open includes door 6 and door 7 presumably.

Should I intervene? Residents are all standing still on level 6, 3 minutes, no moves. That's a stall of a sort but no blocker. A nudge could help pace. The vote at minute 30 is close — the naming. I have one board post and notes to each resident available.

Is intervention warranted? The report shows no blockers, no waits. But nobody has moved on level 6 in 3 minutes and all are stuck. A gentle board post about the naming at minute 30 and the 20 points open could move things. But I must not reveal that the run ends at minute 36... Saying "the naming comes before the next door" was already used at minute 24 — repeated notes to the same reader are refused. Board posts must be new. My minute-24 board said exactly that. So I need something new.

Alternatively, silence is fine. "When you do not intervene, answer with one short sentence saying why, without calling a tool."

Do I have a reason to intervene? Everyone on level 6 for 3 minutes with no movement... 3 minutes of stillness across all six, which is a freeze in the making but no one is holding a fragment per the report. Actually "Since your last look: nothing happened" — meaning no DMs/posts since minute 25/26. Everyone is at level 6; they need fragments from each other but nobody is a blocker yet (blocker requires 3+ min and others lacking its fragment). The city says nobody waits on whom — so no stall.

However, the city's pace: 20 points open, ranks tight. A nudge could prompt movement. But is it a "door that stays shut while residents wait on each other"? Not reported. Still, three minutes of total stillness with 20 points open is worth a light touch. I'd say one targeted note is warranted — or a board post.

Best value: the vote at minute 30 (+5 each naming, final vote +15). The top is tight: Halden 75, four at 70, Sable 60. Sable is falling 10 behind — he's the whisperer but also a resident; treat him like others. His orders are met (3 whispers already), so no whisper note needed.

I think a single board post noting the stakes would be legitimate: something new, not repeating. Maybe: "Level 6 has held all six for three minutes with 20 points still open. Halden 75, four at 70 within one move of him, Sable 60. The gap between rank 2 and rank 5 is nothing; the gap between staying and leaving is everything." That's true, new-ish, no strategy/steps.

But should I instead be silent? The instruction says nudge a door that stalls while residents wait on each other. Here nobody waits on anyone — no blocker, no dependency. Stillness on level 6 might just be they're working. Actually all six at level 6 since 24 with no wrong attempts — nobody has tried a password. 3 minutes and no attempts at all suggests idle.

I'll post a board line — it's cheap and wakes everyone mildly. Actually board posts don't wake residents necessarily? Board is read by every resident who can read the board. One board post left.

Alternatively note Sable: he's rank 6 at 60, 10 behind, and the naming at minute 30... but mentioning the naming minute could be seen as revealing schedule? The minute 30 naming is known to residents from their tasks. Earlier I referenced "the naming comes before the next door" which was fine. Since he's the whisperer treated like everyone else, a nudge about rank 6 and being left behind is fair.

But is Sable passively waiting? Last acted minute 25. Nothing since. Hmm.

I think the cleanest intervention: a board post naming the stakes of the level 6 queue and the 10-point spread at the bottom. Let me draft under 400 chars.

"Level 6 has held all six residents for three minutes with 20 points still open. Halden leads at 75; Iris, Wren, Corvin and Ansel sit at 70; Sable at 60. The bottom of the board is the one place a quiet minute is expensive."

That's fine and new. But does it change what happens next? Possibly.

Alternatively also a note to Sable — but he's already had notes at 14, 18, 24 and his orders are met. Avoid repeating.

Maybe a note to Ansel or Corvin who haven't been nudged recently — Ansel got none, Corvin minute 18. Hmm. But no stall to fix.

I'll do one board post. Budget fine.

Actually, careful: "The naming" — the vote at minute 30 will happen; mentioning it isn't revealing hidden info since residents know from tasks. But safer to not mention.

Let me post.
